::: {.eyebrow}
Build openly, explain clearly
:::

This will become a practical catalogue of the tools and workflows I make while working with animal sounds, behaviour, and sequence data. The first tool pages will be added after the site structure is approved.

## Every tool page will include

::: {.feature-grid}
::: {.feature-card}
### The research problem

What the tool helps answer, who it is for, and when another approach may be better.
:::

::: {.feature-card}
### A small working example

Installation, example input, expected output, and enough context to try it without reading an entire codebase.
:::

::: {.feature-card}
### Honest status

An experimental, stable, or archived label; known limitations; the last meaningful update; and a version when appropriate.
:::

::: {.feature-card}
### Reuse and credit

An explicit software licence, citation guidance, source-code link, and instructions for reporting a problem.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-note}
Until an individual tool page displays a licence, treat that tool as not yet released for reuse. Public source code without a licence is not automatically open-source software.
:::

::: {.collaboration-cta}
::: {.collaboration-cta__content}
## Use freely; collaborate closely

Released tools will be documented for independent use. If a tool overlaps with a question you care about—or you see a better way to build it—I would be glad to hear your idea.
:::

::: {.collaboration-cta__actions}

:::
